title: When prices go up and down
summary: Prices rise and fall over time; an emergency fund helps you avoid being forced to sell.

variants.markdown:
**English draft for R5 review.**

Kabir's uncle watches the prices of a fictional company, Sundar Foods, in a virtual play portfolio. One week the price drops from ₹100 to ₹80, and the family group chat panics.

Prices **move up and down** over time because many people change their minds about what something is worth. A fall on paper is not a loss until it is sold.

Then Kabir's aunt needs ₹20,000 for a hospital bill. With no savings, the family must sell during the fall. That is a **forced sale**, and it locks in the drop.

An **emergency fund** is cash kept aside for surprises. With one, the family never has to sell at a bad moment, and can decide calmly with **time on their side**.

No one can reliably guess the highs and lows. Any example number here is an assumption, not a promise.

Gullak uses virtual play money only.

questions.prompt: Why do prices go up and down?

options.text: Because people's views of value keep changing
Because a bank sets them each day
Because they always follow a fixed pattern

questions.explanation: Prices shift as many people change their view of what something is worth.

questions.prompt: What does an emergency fund help the family avoid?

options.text: Being forced to sell during a fall

questions.explanation: Cash set aside means urgent needs do not force a sale at a bad time.

questions.prompt: Sundar Foods fell from ₹100 to ₹80. What is true?

options.text: The fall is on paper until something is actually sold

questions.explanation: A price fall is only realised as a loss if you sell; time lets you decide calmly.
